new_entities.name: Scalp microneedling
new_entities.description: Microneedling-based scalp treatment used for androgenetic alopecia, often as an adjunct to topical therapy.

new_entities.name: Androgenetic alopecia
new_entities.description: Pattern hair loss in men or women.

edges.effect_quant: Three recent meta-analyses of randomized trials found that adding microneedling to topical therapy improves hair count and diameter more than minoxidil alone, but the evidence mainly reflects adjunctive rather than standalone microneedling. That makes the direction favorable, but not cleanly independent.
edges.population: men and women with androgenetic alopecia receiving scalp microneedling, usually alongside topical minoxidil or another active treatment
edges.mechanism: Microneedling may enhance follicular signaling and topical delivery, which is why its strongest evidence appears in combination protocols rather than as an isolated intervention.
edges.summary: Scalp microneedling has a real supportive signal in androgenetic alopecia, especially as an add-on to minoxidil. The honest framing is adjunctive benefit rather than a proven standalone replacement for established pharmacologic therapy.
edges.caveats: Most of the evidence is combination-based, so this edge should not be read as microneedling alone being fully validated. Protocol heterogeneity is high, and adverse effects, though usually mild, are more common than with topical monotherapy.
